Consult Summary:
- 31-year-old female with 7 days of fever, sweating, myalgia, and malaise following recent travel to Vietnam; no localizing symptoms identified, further evaluation planned.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Fever for 7 days, hot and sweaty, muscle aches, significant fatigue, nausea with reduced oral intake, intermittent chills.
- Associated symptoms: Night sweats, aching muscles, persistent nausea, tiredness; no cough, sore throat, ear pain, diarrhea, neck stiffness, significant new headache, rash, joint swelling/tenderness, dysuria, or urinary frequency.
- Pertinent negatives: No respiratory symptoms, no urinary symptoms, no rash, no recent migraine, no diarrhea, no neck stiffness.
- Past medical history: Chronic back pain (diagnosed as posture-related, under physiotherapy care).
- Medications: Seroxat (dose/route/frequency not documented), ibuprofen (OTC, recommended dose), paracetamol (OTC, recommended dose).
- Allergies: Pollen (hay fever).
- Social history: Works as a nurse, up to date on vaccinations (including Hepatitis B), non-smoker, moderate alcohol intake, moderate physical activity.
- Preventive care: Up to date vaccinations.
- Travel history: Returned from Vietnam 4 weeks ago; took daily malaria prophylaxis (specific medication name not recalled); extensive travel including rural/countryside areas, trekking, cycling, farmland exposure.
- Family history: Father died of heart attack at age 68.

Examination:
- No examination performed or findings documented.

Impression:
- Fever of unknown origin; differential includes possible tropical/exotic infection (including malaria) due to recent travel and exposure.

Plan:
- Advise in-person clinic assessment and physical examination as soon as possible.
- Arrange blood tests: malaria screen (thick and thin blood films), inflammatory markers, other relevant labs as indicated by clinical findings after exam.
- Recommend patient not return to work until further assessment is completed.
- Patient to attend central London clinic today; instructions to call admin for appointment.
- Doctor to document assessment and test recommendations for clinic/A&E reference.

Quality checks:
● Missing but clinically expected elements: No medication dose/route/frequency for Seroxat, ibuprofen, paracetamol; allergy to medications not specifically addressed; no vitals or examination findings.
● No internal conflicts identified.
● Transcript quality: Good, clear and complete clinical content.
